adjudication_rule.statement: One rule, applied identically to all five. (1) Correct every defect found in the contract's inputs -- period mismatches, omitted balance-sheet items, subsequent capital events, sign errors, and unsourced or reverse-engineered judgments -- without changing the model's method or its genuinely sourced judgments. (2) ADMISSIBILITY: a variant is admissible only if it is stated AS OF THE SAME DATE as the market price it is compared against. A variant that describes the enterprise at an earlier date, however internally consistent, is not a candidate answer to 'what is this share worth at today's price'. (3) Recompute the annualized return across the reasonable range of ADMISSIBLE corrected inputs, not one hand-picked variant. (4) The flag is an ARTIFACT only if the corrected result lands INSIDE the +/-25% band across that range. If |return| >= 25% survives the corrections, the flag is REAL, whatever else is wrong with the proof.
adjudication_rule.why_stated: Rev 1 applied two different rules. It called AXTI 'real' because the extremity survived several anchors, then called AXON 'artifact' on a single normalization year -- the only year of three that cleared the band -- while ignoring the other two, which did not. The rule below is rev 1's own stated method (method[3]); rev 2 applies it consistently and the two verdicts move.
adjudication_rule.why_admissibility_clause: Added in this correction pass. Without it the rule is incomplete and AXTI's own variant table contradicts it: the row 'pre-raise book $274.874M / 55,579,000 pre-raise shares' is arithmetically correct, internally consistent, and lands at -30.83%, OUTSIDE the band -- so a literal reading of steps (1) and (3) would have to keep AXTI 'real'. It was excluded in rev 2 only by a prose aside ('describes a company that no longer exists'). The clause makes that exclusion part of the rule: the price is 2026-08-09, so the enterprise must be stated on a post-2026-04-22 (post-raise) basis. The pre-raise row is retained below as diagnostic arithmetic -- it isolates the size of the share-count artifact -- and is marked admissible: false. NOTE: the AXTI headline row (facts_only_cash_restatement) needs no admissibility argument at all; it is inside the band on the contract's own component method with one fact corrected.

defect_classes.name: wrong or incomplete fact
defect_classes.definition: A locked fact is the wrong number for the concept it names, or a balance-sheet concept the method requires is simply absent. Corrected by re-selecting the tag. Instances: AXTI and AXON omitted ShortTermInvestments / MarketableSecurities (XC-6a); AEHR's dropped sign on OperatingIncomeLoss; AEHR's stale net_financial_claims.

defect_classes.name: date mismatch
defect_classes.definition: Two facts that must describe the same enterprise are taken at dates across which the enterprise changed. Corrected by re-dating, and adjudicated under the admissibility clause. Instances: CEG (2026-03-31 post-Calpine sheet vs FY2025 pre-Calpine cash flow, XC-6b); AXON (2026-03-31 sheet vs FY2025 earnings).

defect_classes.name: numerator/denominator mismatch inside one per-share division
defect_classes.definition: The share count and the value being divided are as-of different dates with a capital event in between. Strictly worse than D2 because it survives any fix that only re-dates the balance sheet. Instance: AXTI (XC-8).

defect_classes.name: fabricated judgment
defect_classes.definition: NEW IN THIS CORRECTION PASS. A number presented in the proof as a derived or sourced judgment is in fact a hardcoded constant, typed to reproduce a pre-existing answer and then reverse-engineered into the proof under a technical-sounding label. It is not a wrong FACT, so step (1)'s 'correct the inputs' does not reach it; and it is not a sourced judgment, so 'hold the model's judgments fixed' must not protect it. A fabricated judgment is corrected by REPLACING IT WITH A RANGE of defensible values and testing whether the verdict survives across that range. If the extremity exists only at the fabricated point value, the flag is an artifact. Instances: ABX's 4.0x capitalization multiple (build_abx_contract_proofs.py, base = round(OP_PS * 4.0, 2), re-presented at line 97 as a 4.0027x 'Duration-adjusted reinvestment capitalization multiple'); AXTI's 11.75x 'mid-cycle capacity value multiple', which exists because $1.4009/sh was typed into the LEGACY table (XC-4). AXTI's verdict does not rest on D4 -- it rests on D1 and D3 -- but the same defect is present.

variant_breadth_asymmetry.statement: Variant breadth is NOT applied uniformly across the five, and this is stated here rather than left implicit. AXTI and ABX are adjudicated with ANCHOR REPLACEMENT variants (book equity, revenue and earnings multiples substituted for the published component set). AXON and CEG are adjudicated with FACTS-ONLY variants (the published model, judgments and multiples held exactly fixed; only the locked facts re-selected or re-dated). AEHR gets both.
variant_breadth_asymmetry.why_it_is_asymmetric: It follows the defect class, not a considered choice about evidence standard. Where the defect is D1/D2/D3 the published method survives correction and facts-only variants are the natural test (AXON, CEG). Where the defect is D4 the published method cannot be held fixed -- holding it fixed IS holding the fabricated number fixed -- so anchor replacement is the only available test (ABX). AXTI was adjudicated with anchor replacement in rev 1 and rev 2 carried that framing forward even though AXTI's decisive defects are D1 and D3, for which a facts-only variant exists and is stronger. That is corrected below: AXTI's headline is now the facts-only row.
variant_breadth_asymmetry.no_verdict_turns_on_it: Checked, not assumed. Applying an ABX-style audited-book anchor to AXON -- the ticker where anchor replacement was NOT used -- gives StockholdersEquity $3,242.658M at 2025-12-31 / 80.602077M shares = $40.2305/sh and -32.14%, and $3,534.113M at 2026-03-31 / 80.602077M = $43.8464/sh and -31.30%. Both are outside the band and both are worse than the -31.04% three-year facts-only variant, so AXON stays real on either breadth. CEG's facts-only correction already clears the band at -18.72%, so adding anchors cannot make it real. The asymmetry changes no verdict; it is recorded because an adjudication that varies its evidence breadth by ticker without saying so is the exact failure rev 2 charged rev 1 with.

cross_cutting_findings.title: The fact ledger pairs a post-capital-event share count with a pre-capital-event balance sheet, and nothing looks at Subsequent Events
cross_cutting_findings.detail: shares_outstanding is taken from dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding via ENTITY_SHARE_SPECS / _select_share_companyfact in automate_valuation_readiness.py (currently :172-175 and :191; cite the symbols, the lines drift), whose as_of is the FILING COVER DATE (AXTI 2026-05-04, AXON 2026-04-30, CEG 2026-04-30), while cash_m, debt_m and equity come from the BALANCE-SHEET date (2026-03-31). Any equity issuance, buyback, or debt raise between those two dates enters the denominator and never enters the numerator, and the compiler has no reader for the Subsequent Events note that discloses it. AXTI is a clean, EXACTLY reconciling demonstration: the 424B5's own base of 55,578,827 shares outstanding at 2026-04-20 plus the 8,560,311 + 1,284,046 shares sold on 2026-04-22 equals 65,423,184 -- to the share, the cover count the contract divides by, and the same figure the prospectus itself projects as shares outstanding immediately after the offering 'if the underwriter exercises its option to purchase additional shares in full'. (The XBRL us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding tag at 2026-03-31 reads 55,579,000, a thousands-rounded value; the 173-share gap against 55,578,827 is that rounding and nothing else. Rev 2 attributed it to option/RSU settlement noise, which was wrong.) The $600.2M of net proceeds those shares bought is 2.2x the entire book equity of the balance sheet being divided, and $9.17 of the $65.27 share price. This is a strictly more dangerous version of XC-6(b): XC-6(b) mismatches two dates, XC-8 mismatches a numerator and a denominator inside the SAME per-share division, so it survives any fix that only re-dates the balance sheet. A guard belongs next to the fact-ledger builder: if the shares_outstanding as_of post-dates the cash_m / debt_m as_of, either re-select shares at the balance-sheet date or refuse to lock until the intervening period is reconciled.

rule_application.defect_class: D4 -- fabricated judgment. This is stated explicitly because rev 2's own rule did not reach ABX and the verdict was therefore unreasoned. Step (1) permits correcting INPUTS 'without changing the model's method, judgments, discount rate or terminal multiple', yet ABX is adjudicated by varying the capitalization multiple and substituting audited book -- i.e. by changing exactly what step (1) said to hold fixed. The resolution is not that ABX is an exception; it is that ABX's defect is not a wrong FACT at all. Its facts (FY2025 operating income $88.757M, revenue $235.2M, debt $291.844M, equity $418.54M, 99.2M shares) reproduce from the filings. What is wrong is a JUDGMENT that was never made: build_abx_contract_proofs.py contains the typed constant base = round(OP_PS * 4.0, 2), and line 97 then computes mult = LEGACY['life_solutions_engine'][case] / OP_PS and reports the quotient, 4.0027x, in the proof as a 'Duration-adjusted reinvestment capitalization multiple'. The label describes a derivation that does not exist. Nothing in the 10-K, the transcripts or the method registry supports 4x.
rule_application.why_the_judgment_shield_does_not_apply: Holding 'the model's judgments' fixed is what makes a facts-only correction a fair test: it prevents an adjudicator from manufacturing whatever answer it wants by re-picking multiples. That protection is owed to a judgment that was actually exercised and can be argued with. It is not owed to a constant typed to reproduce a pre-existing legacy answer and then dressed as a derivation -- protecting that converts the rule into a guarantee that any sufficiently fabricated proof is un-adjudicable. So for D4 the correction is not 'replace the fact', it is 'replace the point value with a RANGE of defensible values and test whether the verdict survives across the range' (adjudication_rule.defect_classes D4).
rule_application.corrected_range: Replacing the fabricated 4.0x with a range: 6x gives $3.08/sh and -16.49%; 8x gives $4.87/sh and -10.84%; audited book equity ($418.54M / 99.2M shares = $4.2192/sh) gives -12.63%. The published 4.0x itself gives $1.2901/sh and -26.24%.
rule_application.conclusion: To stay outside the band the equity must be worth less than $1.4496/sh -- below 0.35x audited book, and below 4.5x FY2025 pre-tax consolidated operating income. Only the typed 4.0x delivers that; every other point in the range is inside the band, and the extremity therefore exists ONLY at the fabricated value. Under adjudication_rule as amended (D4: an extremity that survives nowhere except at the fabricated point value is an artifact), ABX is an artifact. Note that this is a weaker-sounding but more honest verdict than rev 2's: the claim is not that ABX is worth $3.08 or $4.22, it is that NOTHING in the proof establishes that ABX is worth less than $1.4496, which is what the flag asserts.
rule_application.variant_breadth_note: ABX is adjudicated by anchor replacement rather than facts-only. Under D4 that is forced, not chosen: a facts-only variant holds the fabricated multiple fixed and can only ever return -26.24%. See adjudication_rule.variant_breadth_asymmetry.

tickers.root_cause: The extremity is produced by a single undocumented judgment: a 4.0x capitalization multiple on FY2025 CONSOLIDATED PRE-TAX operating income, hardcoded as base = round(OP_PS * 4.0, 2) in the LEGACY module constant of build_abx_contract_proofs.py (currently :42) and then reverse-engineered back into the proof as a 4.0027x 'Duration-adjusted reinvestment capitalization multiple' by the mult = LEGACY[...] / OP_PS quotient in the life_solutions_engine builder (currently :97). Defect class D4. The component is declared method_id owner_earnings_reinvestment_dcf but performs no discounting. Nothing in the filing supports 4x rather than 6x or 8x, and the choice is the whole answer. Two further asymmetries push the same way. (1) The model subtracts 100% of the $291.844M of reported debt (Q1 2026) but explicitly declines to carry the life-settlement policy portfolio as an asset ('policy portfolio fair-value marks flow through earnings, not a separate additive NAV layer', build_abx_contract_proofs.py:130) -- so the debt that funds the portfolio is counted and the fair-value-marked portfolio behind $902.2M of total assets and $418.5M of book equity is not. That is the WHK failure mode in corrections.md, inverted. (2) longevity_and_funding_reserve then charges another -$59.5M partly for 'credit spread widening on ABXL notes', a second bite at the same credit claim. Separately, the anchor itself is questionable in both directions: FY2025 operating income of $88.757M on $235.2M of revenue (37.7% margin) against only $25.68M of operating cash flow means most of that 'income' is non-cash fair-value marks, and the issuer's own cash is lumpy (Q1 2026 OCF $91.7M vs FY2025 $25.7M). The contract's own second method, run on real filing cash flow, returned -2.4% -- a 24-point disagreement recorded as confirmation.

(1) NET FINANCIAL POSITION IS ONE-SIDED. The proof adds cash of $471.156M (us-gaap:CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents at 2026-03-31) and subtracts $1,730.987M of LongTermDebtNoncurrent, producing an equity value of $263.206M. At that same date the same companyfacts file reports ShortTermInvestments $260.000M and MarketableSecurities $18.052M -- $278.052M more than the proof used, and larger than the equity value it produces (XC-6a). (2) THE BALANCE SHEET DOES NOT MATCH THE EARNINGS PERIOD. normalized_owner_earnings_m is an FY2025 figure ending 2025-12-31, but cash and debt are locked at 2026-03-31 -- exactly the defect rev 1 correctly diagnosed for CEG and then never applied here. Across that quarter cash + short-term investments + marketable securities fell from $1,746.023M to $749.208M, -57.1%, so the two defects together move the net financial position from +$15.853M to -$1,259.831M, a $1.276B swing on a business whose whole modelled equity value is $263M. Attributing that swing correctly: the DATE alone, holding the cash side complete, moves it from +$15.853M (2025-12-31) to -$981.779M (2026-03-31), a $997.6M swing; the remaining $278.052M is the one-sided cash tag (XC-6a), which omits ShortTermInvestments $260.000M and MarketableSecurities $18.052M at 2026-03-31. Rev 2 attributed the whole $1.276B to 'the date choice alone', which double-counted the cash-tag defect into the date defect. On the date-matched 2025-12-31 sheet the SAME FY2025 base gives $19.0924/sh and -39.00% -- not the $6.72 / -47.45% rev 1 published as the cash correction. (3) THE EARNINGS BASE IS DISPUTABLE BUT NOT DEMONSTRABLY A TROUGH. FY2025 owner earnings of $75.081M (OCF $211.339M - capex $136.258M) are well below FY2024's $329.527M. Rev 1's trough argument also leaned on evidence that does not survive checking: Q1 2026 net income of $169.312M is real, but us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss for the same quarter is only $29.243M, so the figure is dominated by non-operating items -- and FY2025 shows the same pattern in reverse, with a -$62.076M operating LOSS against $124.656M of net income. Most decisively, Q1 2026 operating cash flow was -$31.517M against $23.125M of capex: on the very measure the model capitalizes, the quarter after the alleged trough was -$54.6M. (4) Secondary defects, unchanged from rev 1 and all still real: shares_m is dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding at 2026-04-30, a basic cover-page count, but is labelled 'Diluted shares' (and post-dates the balance sheet -- XC-8); $1.731B of convertible notes is charged at face with no offsetting conversion shares, counted once as debt and never as dilution; and the locked fact's locator names us-gaap:NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities ($211.339M) for a value of $75.081M (XC-6c). (5) One rev 1 claim withdrawn: the parenthetical that Axon 'also carried $1,733.777M of AvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebtSecurities at 2025-12-31, so the true net financial position is nowhere near -$1.26B' should not be used as an additive asset. $1,733.777M is the AFS fair-value disclosure and overlaps the $1,213.393M of cash and equivalents, $505.417M of short-term investments and $27.213M of marketable securities already counted (those three total $1,746.023M). Adding it would double-count. The corrected net financial position at 2025-12-31 is +$15.853M, not +$1.7B.

rule_application.share_reconciliation: EXACT, and the residual is explained rather than waved at. The 424B5 prospectus supplement dated 2026-04-21 states the share count both before and after the offering: 'The number of shares of common stock that will be outstanding after this offering as shown above is based on 55,578,827 shares of common stock issued and outstanding as of April 20, 2026', and 'Shares of Common Stock to be Outstanding Immediately After this Offering: 64,139,138 shares of common stock (or 65,423,184 shares if the underwriter exercises its option to purchase additional shares in full)'.
